mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines skeletal muscle and distinguishes it from smooth muscle?

options.A: Skeletal muscle is voluntary, multinucleated, striated; smooth muscle is involuntary, non‑striated, spindle‑shaped
options.B: Skeletal muscle is involuntary, non‑striated; smooth muscle is voluntary, striated
options.C: Both are voluntary and striated, but skeletal muscle has intercalated discs
options.D: Skeletal muscle lacks sarcomeres while smooth muscle has them

mcqs.answer: Skeletal muscle is voluntary, multinucleated, striated; smooth muscle is involuntary, non‑striated, spindle‑shaped
mcqs.explanation: Skeletal muscle fibers are long, cylindrical, multinucleated and show transverse striations; they are under voluntary CNS control. Smooth muscle fibers are spindle‑shaped, have a single nucleus, lack striations and are controlled involuntarily by the autonomic nervous system. Options B, C and D contain incorrect statements.

mcqs.question: Which physiological process primarily depends on the contraction of smooth muscle?

options.A: Flexing the forearm at the elbow
options.B: Peristaltic movement of food through the intestine
options.C: Ejection of blood from the ventricles

mcqs.answer: Peristaltic movement of food through the intestine
mcqs.explanation: Smooth muscle lines the walls of hollow viscera such as the gastrointestinal tract, where coordinated, slow contractions produce peristalsis. Flexing the forearm uses skeletal muscle, blood ejection uses cardiac muscle, and eyebrow movement also uses skeletal muscle. Hence option B is correct.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes a characteristic of cardiac muscle?

options.A: It is found only in the heart, is striated, involuntary and possesses intercalated discs
options.B: It is multinucleated, voluntary and lacks striations
options.C: It is non‑striated, voluntary and contains dense bodies
options.D: It is found in the walls of blood vessels and contracts rapidly under conscious control

mcqs.answer: It is found only in the heart, is striated, involuntary and possesses intercalated discs
mcqs.explanation: Cardiac muscle cells are striated like skeletal muscle but are involuntary and have unique intercalated discs that allow rapid impulse propagation. They are typically mononucleated and located only in the heart. Options B, C and D describe incorrect features.

mcqs.question: A patient suffers from a neurological disorder that impairs voluntary movement but leaves heart rate unchanged. Which type of muscle is most likely affected?
mcqs.explanation: Skeletal muscle is under voluntary control of the somatic nervous system; damage to this pathway impairs voluntary movements while cardiac muscle (involuntary, autonomic control) and smooth muscle (also involuntary) continue to function. Therefore skeletal muscle is the affected type.

mcqs.question: True or false: Skeletal muscles can relax completely without any nerve stimulation.
mcqs.explanation: Skeletal muscle relaxation requires cessation of neural stimulation and active calcium re‑uptake; however, a minimal basal tone is maintained by spontaneous motor unit activity. Complete relaxation without any nerve input does not occur under normal physiological conditions. Hence the statement is false.

mcqs.question: Why does smooth muscle contract more slowly and sustain longer contractions compared to skeletal muscle?

options.A: It contains dense bodies and lacks organized sarcomeres, leading to slower cross‑bridge cycling
options.B: It has a higher mitochondrial density that slows contraction
options.C: It possesses intercalated discs that delay impulse transmission
options.D: Its fibers are multinucleated, causing delayed contraction

mcqs.answer: It contains dense bodies and lacks organized sarcomeres, leading to slower cross‑bridge cycling
mcqs.explanation: Smooth muscle cells lack the regular sarcomeric arrangement of skeletal muscle; instead, actin filaments are anchored to dense bodies, resulting in slower, more sustained contractions. Options B, C, and D describe features not characteristic of smooth muscle or unrelated to contraction speed.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly compares cardiac muscle with skeletal muscle?

options.B: Cardiac muscle has intercalated discs, which are absent in skeletal muscle
options.C: Skeletal muscle fibers are branched, whereas cardiac fibers are long and unbranched
options.D: Cardiac muscle lacks striations, unlike skeletal muscle

mcqs.answer: Cardiac muscle has intercalated discs, which are absent in skeletal muscle
mcqs.explanation: Intercalated discs are specialized junctions unique to cardiac muscle that facilitate synchronized contraction. Skeletal muscle lacks these structures. Both muscle types are striated, but skeletal muscle is voluntary and unbranched, while cardiac muscle is involuntary and branched. Options A, C, and D are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which statement accurately describes the control mechanisms of the three muscle types?

options.A: Skeletal muscle – voluntary CNS control; Smooth muscle – involuntary autonomic control; Cardiac muscle – hormonal control only
options.B: Skeletal muscle – involuntary autonomic control; Smooth muscle – voluntary CNS control; Cardiac muscle – voluntary control
options.C: Skeletal muscle – voluntary CNS control; Smooth muscle – involuntary autonomic control; Cardiac muscle – involuntary autonomic control with intrinsic pacemaker activity
options.D: All three muscle types are controlled solely by the endocrine system

mcqs.answer: Skeletal muscle – voluntary CNS control; Smooth muscle – involuntary autonomic control; Cardiac muscle – involuntary autonomic control with intrinsic pacemaker activity
mcqs.explanation: Skeletal muscle contracts under voluntary somatic nervous system input. Smooth muscle is regulated by the autonomic nervous system and various hormones. Cardiac muscle also receives autonomic input but possesses its own pacemaker cells (SA node) that generate rhythmic impulses. Option C correctly captures these mechanisms; the other options contain inaccurate control descriptions.
